title: Background tasks

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
FastAPI builds JSON APIs that web and mobile applications call over HTTP; type annotations help validate inputs and describe the API contract.
PURPOSE AND REAL-WORLD USE

FastAPI `BackgroundTasks` schedules short work in the same process after the response is sent, such as recording a lightweight notification. Long or durable work belongs in a task queue. This demo writes to an in-memory list, which is not persistent.

To run these examples locally, install `pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx` plus any extra package named in the lesson. Save the server example as `app.py` and start `uvicorn app:app --reload`. `--reload` is for development only.

WHERE DOES THIS APPEAR IN REAL LIFE?
Recording a small analytics event without delaying the response.
If this part is omitted: Running optional work synchronously in the request can unnecessarily delay the client response.

LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, FastAPI` — Imports a required type or tool; without it, the name is unavailable.
`app = FastAPI()` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`completed_messages = []` — Continues the application's data handling or control flow.
`def record_message(message: str):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`completed_messages.append(message)` — Runs work for this request; its result or side effect affects the response.
`@app.post("/notify")` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`def notify(message: str, tasks: BackgroundTasks):` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`tasks.add_task(record_message, message)` — Runs work for this request; its result or side effect affects the response.
`return {"accepted": True}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.

COMMON MISTAKES
Assuming an in-memory background task is durable or retried; its work is lost if the process stops.

spans.title: Practical tip
spans.text: Keep `BackgroundTasks` for short work and tell the client what was accepted in the response.

spans.title: One level deeper
spans.text: A separate worker queue can add retries, monitoring, and throttling for long work; `BackgroundTasks` does not provide these automatically.

spans.title: Important warning
spans.text: Do not rely on an in-process callback for critical email, payments, or work that must not be lost.
QUICK RECALL
Question: Which action best prevents the common mistake from this lesson?
Answer: Keep `BackgroundTasks` for short work and tell the client what was accepted in the response.
